why: Story 6.11, the negative direction: a setup.install command that fails is an INFRASTRUCTURE error and must never be reported as a product FAIL. The declared install exits 7, and the run must end with an infraError outcome at exit 3, with the gates stage SKIPPED rather than FAILED. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ASSERTION THIS STORY MAKES. A missing or broken install tells you nothing whatever about the branch under verification: exit 1 would assert that the branch has defects on no evidence at all, blocking a mergeable branch or sending a developer hunting a bug that does not exist, and a verification gate that blames the branch for a broken registry is switched off within a week. Exit 3 says SpecWitness could not reach a conclusion, which is what happened. It is the exact mirror of fixture 07-broken-build, which must never report an infrastructure error. THE FIXTURE MUST ALSO FAIL FOR ITS STATED REASON: the gate exits zero on any tree and the probe reads a committed file, so nothing else here can produce a non-PASS outcome -- which means that under the placeholder this story replaced, where the setup stage spawned nothing and reported ok, this fixture would reach PASS at exit 0. Pinning exit 3 is therefore pinning that the install ran AND that its failure was classified as infrastructure. The evidence block is exact with only 'command': the setup stage records the failed install as command evidence before it throws, and the ABSENCE of a 'gate' kind is how this file pins structurally that the gates stage never ran -- a skipped stage and a passed stage look identical in a criteria set, and only one of them is true here. 'criteria' is exact-and-empty for the same reason fixture 08 is: an InfraError breaks the stage loop, so the aggregate stage never runs and no criterion result is materialised. Any criterion appearing here would mean the pipeline kept going after it had lost the environment. Exit 7 rather than 1 is deliberate, so the message pins the child's real exit status rather than a normalised one. AMENDED BY HAND on 2026-09-05, during story 6.11's own review round, and the reason is recorded here because a changed expectation is the one edit this directory must be able to explain: a review found that two failure arms named neither the declared command nor the config key, the product's messages were changed to name both, and this file's stderr expectations were rewritten by hand to the new strings. The expectation moved because the PRODUCT deliberately improved, which is one of the two answers a red fixture can have -- it was not regenerated, and the assertions are now stronger than they were, pinning the ERROR/HINT pair and the config key an operator has to open.
